belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: Under the sole hypothesis that each c_i is C^{1,1}, the tie sets {c_i - c_j = w_i - w_j} can have positive Lebesgue measure. Example within the hypotheses: take u in C^{1,1}(Omega), not identically zero, vanishing on a closed set K of positive measure (such functions exist, e.g. built from a fat Cantor set), and set c_1 = C + u, c_2 = C with C > sup|u|, so both costs are nonnegative C^{1,1} functions; with w_1 = w_2 the tie set contains K. Then the two Laguerre cells intersect on a positive-measure set, and since c_1 = c_2 on K, the mass of K can be assigned to either seed at equal cost, giving many optimal partition maps. Hence the claimed uniqueness of the solution T and the zero-measure-intersection property both fail as stated; the cited semi-discrete results assume extra conditions (e.g. nonvanishing gradient of c_i - c_j a.e. on tie sets) that are not imported here.

failure_location.quote: The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with the standard additional hypothesis from the cited semi-discrete literature (e.g. for all i != j the difference c_i - c_j has a.e. nonvanishing gradient on tie sets, or all tie sets have measure zero); the costs used in the paper satisfy it.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's uniqueness and null-intersection guarantees are unproved in degenerate cases; the well-definedness of the partition on which the whole framework rests holds only under an unstated nondegeneracy hypothesis.
issues.title: Theorem 1: uniqueness of the Monge map and zero-measure cell intersections fail without a nondegeneracy hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis restores the statement; the paper's applications use distinct power-law costs whose tie sets are smooth curves, so no method, conclusion or downstream result is affected.

issues.failure_explanation: The Laguerre cells (eq:Laguerre), hence the volume constraints (eq:laguerrevolume), are invariant under the global shift (w_i) -> (w_i + t) for any t in R: every admissible weight vector comes with a one-parameter family of admissible vectors giving identical cells and volumes. The weights are therefore never uniquely defined; at best they are unique up to an additive constant. The closing sentence promising solvers 'the unique vector of optimal values for the Kantorovitch potentials' inherits the same inaccuracy.

issues.title: Kantorovich weights are not 'uniquely defined' (global additive constant)

issues.failure_explanation: For alpha in (0,2), the function y -> |y - x_i|^alpha is not C^{1,1} at y = x_i: its gradient is unbounded or undefined for alpha <= 1 and only Hölder continuous for 1 < alpha < 2. Theorem thm:semidiscrete is stated only for C^{1,1} costs, yet the paper relies on it for the sub-quadratic power costs that define its central 'soft' regime: eq:powercost is used for any alpha > 0, the bubbly tessellation uses alpha_i in [0.5,4], the falling-sphere and micropipette experiments use alpha = 0.75 and alpha <= 1, and the active-Brownian and crowd-motion experiments use alpha = 0.5. For these costs the existence, uniqueness and volume-constrained Laguerre structure invoked throughout are not covered by the theorem as stated; they do hold (tie sets are smooth curves of measure zero) but only via the more general semi-discrete theory.

issues.failure_explanation: Two gaps. (i) The statement omits the volume constraint: read literally, the unconstrained minimizer of the individual energy is the empty set (energy 0), which is not of the form {c <= w} with w > 0; the constraint |S| = v_i appears only inside the proof. (ii) Even with the constraint, monotonicity of U with U(0) = 0 and U(infty) = 1 does not yield a unique w* with U(w*) = v_i: U(0) = |{c = 0}| can be positive, U jumps if a level set {c(.,x_i) = t} has positive measure (then no w realizes v_i and the level-set characterization fails — e.g. c(.,x_i) vanishing on a ball of volume larger than v_i, where every volume-v_i subset of the ball is a minimizer and none is a level set), and plateaus of U destroy uniqueness. The proof silently needs every level set of c(.,x_i) to have zero Lebesgue measure.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's convention varphi = -log c, adding f(delta) = -delta_+ <= 0 to varphi multiplies the cost by exp(beta delta_+) >= 1 in up-gradient directions: the cost is increased there, not 'the potential lowered ... allowing deformations'. Since a cell is the sublevel set {c <= w} with w fixed by its volume (Lemma lemma:prefferedshape), the cell retracts in up-gradient directions and, by volume conservation, expands down-gradient; its barycenter shifts down-gradient, so the barycenter-seeking centroid dynamics moves the cell away from the chemo-attractant — the opposite of the claimed chemotactic migration. The same sign error makes the gloss of eq:perturbfan ('a larger cost ... even larger for negative gradient') false (positive f lowers c, which would elongate the cell along rather than orthogonal to the gradient), and makes the random 'protrusions' (f = -sum xi_k G <= 0) raise the cost at the designated angles, producing indentations instead of protrusions. All stated behaviours are consistent only if the perturbation is added to +log c (equivalently c -> c_0 exp(+beta f)).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign convention, e.g. define varphi = +log c (or change the signs of f in eq:perturblong, eq:perturbfan and in the protrusion model); after this local change the formulas match the claimed behaviours.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the chemotaxis and random-protrusion models produce the reverse of the claimed qualitative behaviour (migration down the attractant gradient; dents instead of protrusions), contradicting the figure and video descriptions of these experiments.

issues.why_classification: A one-sign local repair makes the construction consistent with every stated claim; no experiment, guarantee or other section is lost. It is not a pure typo because equivalent alternative repairs exist and the surrounding reasoning itself embodies the wrong sign.

Since the morphological changes are biased in the direction of increasing gradient, this choice induces chemotactic migration.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, T_{c_0}(hat mu) is the optimal transport cost for the base L^2 cost; it depends only on the positions and volumes, and by the quoted envelope formula its gradient is the barycenter pull of the c_0-optimal Laguerre cells. The biased cost c = c_0 exp(-beta f(delta u)) does not enter T_{c_0}(hat mu) at all, so the displayed dynamics is insensitive to the chemo-attractant and cannot 'induce chemotactic migration' from the biased morphologies. The intended force — the barycenter pull over the current biased-cost Laguerre cell — is not nabla_{x_i} T_{c_0}(hat mu): the envelope identity requires the cells to be optimal for the same cost that is differentiated, and with cells optimal for c != c_0 the barycenter-pull field is not even the gradient of a transport cost. The equation therefore misdefines the model; the same mismatched notation recurs in the random-protrusion equation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the force explicitly as the barycenter pull over the current (biased-cost) Laguerre cells, e.g. dot x_i = tau int_{L_i} (x - x_i) dx, or use the full gradient nabla_{x_i} T_c(hat mu) of the biased cost; these are different dynamics, so a choice must be made.
issues.overall_effect: The defining equation of the chemotaxis model is inconsistent with the mechanism the section claims to implement; taken literally, the perturbation deforms the displayed shapes without affecting the motion at all.
issues.title: Chemotaxis centroid dynamics as written does not depend on the cost perturbation
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition of one model equation restores consistency with the claimed mechanism; the intended simulations and qualitative conclusions are preserved without new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed Ornstein–Uhlenbeck SDE d xi_k = -xi_k dt + dB^k_t with unconstrained Brownian motion has a Gaussian invariant law supported on all of R, so xi_k takes negative values with positive probability: the stated invariant xi_k >= 0 is not preserved. As written the model does not implement its own amplitude constraint; a confinement mechanism (reflection at zero, truncation) or signed amplitudes must be specified, and the choice matters because under the paper's cost convention a negative xi_k produces retraction rather than protrusion.

\[\cos\theta = \frac{\gamma_{ij}}{2\gamma_0}.\]

issues.failure_explanation: The stated internalization condition gamma_bo < gamma_bw - gamma_ow is contradicted by the caption's own parameters: gamma_bw - gamma_ow = 7 - 30 = -23, so the condition reads 5 < -23, which is false. It is also physically backwards: with the Young–Dupré balance of Lemma lemma:celldoublet, spreading of blue over orange (internalization of the orange population, as shown in the video and in the identical-parameter engulfment experiment) requires a positive spreading coefficient, gamma_ow > gamma_bw + gamma_bo, equivalently gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw, which the parameters do satisfy (5 < 23). As written, the inequality is the condition for the opposite engulfment direction (blue internalized by orange) and is inconsistent with the experiment it labels.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw (equivalently gamma_ow > gamma_bw + gamma_bo), the standard complete-wetting/engulfment condition, which matches the reported parameters and outcome.
issues.overall_effect: The parameter regime under which the model is claimed to reproduce homophilic sorting with internalization is misidentified; the stated DITH condition cannot be satisfied by the reported configuration and inverts the comparison with the classical theory.
issues.title: Internalization condition in the cell-sorting caption is sign-swapped and contradicted by its own parameters
issues.why_classification: The correction swaps two subscripts in one inequality; the experiment itself is consistent with the corrected condition and no result, regime or guarantee is lost.
